# wsp-kit by Aurem

> wsp-kit by Aurem is an engineering tool for small models. It tries to fix small open-weight models by editing their weights directly — no retraining, no fine-tuning, no gradients. An eval gate decides whether any edit ships. Free and open source (MIT).

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/AuremHQ/weight-space-programming/blob/main/README.md): what the kit is, real run numbers, how it works, honest limits
- [SKILL.md](https://github.com/AuremHQ/weight-space-programming/blob/main/SKILL.md): the weight-space programming skill — 3-step workflow, refusal rules, eval gate
- [RESEARCH.md](https://github.com/AuremHQ/weight-space-programming/blob/main/RESEARCH.md): the MIT CSAIL research this builds on, all 8 experiments, honest limits
- [REAL-RUNS.md](https://github.com/AuremHQ/weight-space-programming/blob/main/REAL-RUNS.md): our real-model runs (Qwen3-0.6B, GPT2-124M, SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct) with full numbers
- [Kit README](https://github.com/AuremHQ/weight-space-programming/blob/main/kit/README.md): install and run the kit, CLI and MCP tools
- [Install](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AuremHQ/weight-space-programming/main/install.sh): one-command skill installer

## Facts

- Name: wsp-kit by Aurem. Team: Ora by Aurem (https://auremcto.com). Founder: Tejinder Sandhu.
- License: MIT. Price: free for everyone.
- Models: small open-weight models only, up to 3 billion parameters. Closed API models are refused by design.
- Method: diagnose the failure in the weights, then subtract the failure direction from MLP output columns or dampen them (under 1% of weights), and re-test with an eval gate.
- Gate: an edit ships only if the failing metric improves by at least 5 points with no more than 2 points regression on guards and neighbours, at serving temperature and greedy.
- Real results so far (REAL-RUNS.md, 5 Nov 2026): 7 real-model runs, 2 passed the eval gate, 5 were refused with 0 weights shipped. Passes: SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct (subtraction, layer 23, 129,897 weights, failing 76.11 → 85.56) and Qwen3-0.6B narrow animals eval (dampening 0.25, layers 27 and 26, 131,072 weights, failing 37.78 → 67.22). Both are one failure type: 60-item list looping. Refused: Qwen3-0.6B (4 runs) and GPT2-124M (1 run). The pipeline test on a synthetic model also passed (failing 64.14 → 75.43). Not peer-reviewed.
- Last updated: 7 November 2026.
- Source: https://github.com/AuremHQ/weight-space-programming
- Website: https://auremhq.github.io/weight-space-programming/
